LESSON: ANIMAL REARING PROJECT

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Animal Production
Topic 2.5: Animal Rearing Project
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Animal Rearing Project, part of Animal Production in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How can animal rearing project be carried be out? 2. How do you determine the initial startup cost for a selected animal rearing project?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Animal Rearing Project together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Love: learner develops caring attitude towards others when sharing roles during management of the animal rearing

project.

● Social justice: learner fosters fairness and justice by sharing roles equitably when managing the animal rearing

project.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Life skills: learner develops negotiation skills when discussing a budget proposal on animal rearing project with the

teacher and school administration for approval.

● Financial literacy: learner prepares a reasonable budget resource allocation as learners develop project details and

budget for the animal rearing project.

Suggested Learning Resources:

• Digital devices with assistive technology

• Print materials

• Braille materials

• Appropriate rearing structures such as rabbit hatch, poultry house,

• Feeders and waterers

• Animal feeds

• Livestock production tools and equipment such as ropes, burdizzzo, hoof cutter,

• Tools and equipment such as claw hammer, hand saw, panga, claw bar

• Construction materials such as wood planks, post, poles, nails, iron sheets, wiremesh, hinges

Suggested Key Skills

Carry out routine management practices in an animal rearing project.
